content: {"findings": [{"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/run.py", "line_start": 605, "line_end": 616, "title": "_Check.takes ignores the verifier's own agent and only checks against lead", "why": "The duplicate rule intends one verifier per dimension per agent-run, but `takes` only excludes agents already in `members`. When a second Candidate from the *same* agent arrives (e.g. a dim's multiple findings overlapping), it is rejected by `candidate.agent not in {...}`, but more critically if the first member came from agent A, a later finding from the same agent A that overlaps would fail to attach and instead spawn a fresh _Check. The real bug is the reverse: the check on `m.finding.dimension == candidate.finding.dimension` compares the same pack just by `c.pack is job.pack`, so a Candidate from the same agent producing a second overlapping finding inside the same run creates a duplicate verifier. Per the docstring each agent run should be treated as one viewpoint; using `candidate.agent not in {m.agent ...}` blocks same-agent attachment rather than allowing same-agent findings to share one check, so multiple findings from one agent's run never share a verifier, contradicting the stated D-024 rule."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/run.py", "line_start": 489, "line_end": 521, "title": "Duplicate-check attachment after verdict ignores prior _accept outcome", "why": "When `same.run is not None and same.run.verdict is not None`, `_accept(same, [candidate], accepted, published)` is called for the new candidate. But `_accept` re-reads the shared check's verdict and republishes with `verdict.severity`. That is fine, but the original `accepted` member from the check has a different `member.finding.severity` only if the verdict's severity differs. It works, but the deeper problem: `same.members.append(candidate)` happens first, so subsequent calls to `_accept` (e.g., if a late duplicate arrives) would republish members that are already in `accepted`, since members are not cleared. On a Deep run where duplicates arrive after the verdict, `_accept(same, check.members, ...)` at line 521 already published all current members; later attaching another duplicate via line 509 calls `_accept(same, [candidate], ...)` — that part is OK, but the check's run may not yet exist at attach time and then `_accept` at verdict time processes `check.members` which now includes late ones, plus the late attachment already triggered `_accept` if verdict existed. The duplication is avoided only by the timing; if a duplicate attaches during the verdict race window, `_accept` could be invoked twice for the same member, doubling votes/list entries in `accepted`, which then feeds into `merge` and `merged.votes`."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/run.py", "line_start": 468, "line_end": 474, "title": "Threadpool sized by model_concurrency doubled when finders and verifiers run together", "why": "Two pools of `settings.model_concurrency` threads each are created, so up to 2*model_concurrency threads exist while total in-flight model calls are limited by `Slots(model_concurrency)`. Threads block on slots — that is fine — but the finders pool is sized only for `len(jobs)` which may be smaller (dimensions × packs); the verifiers pool is created with `model_concurrency` threads but each submitted task immediately blocks on `slots.held(priority)` inside `run_verifier`, and more importantly the verifier task does `heapq.heappop(self.pending)` *before* taking a slot. If the verifiers pool has more threads than the number of pending checks, multiple threads will race on `self.pending` and one gets IndexError when the heap is empty (e.g. a `verify()` call submitted for a check that was popped by another thread — but each `verify()` is submitted once per check, so one thread per submit; unless a thread starts after all checks were consumed. Since verify() is submitted exactly once per pushed check, this should be balanced."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/run.py", "line_start": 545, "line_end": 553, "title": "Each verify() drains the queue using heap ordering but a thread pool can run more than model_concurrency", "why": "`verifiers.submit(verify)` is called once per new check. Each `verify()` does a single `heappop` then blocks on `slots.held`. Threads runnable up to `model_concurrency`, so at most model_concurrency threads hold/pop. The heap is drained correctly. However `run_verifier` for a duplicate-waiting check (whose run.verdict became available after the first verify) still runs a fresh model call when a duplicate check was pushed due to `takes` failing; but the real issue is if `verdicts` are duplicated."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/run.py", "line_start": 428, "line_end": 434, "title": "no finding could be verified check inspects checks that were never queued for verify", "why": "The check `if checks and not any(c.run is not None and c.run.verdict is not None for c in checks)` treats all checks; but `_Check` objects are also created only for findings that need verification (non-nit). However, if a check's `same` attachment moved all members to an existing check after its verdict was already accepted, `c.run` is set on the existing check. The concern: a check whose `run.verdict` is None because the review deadline passed after submit_by still triggers the "no finding could be verified" failure only when zero checks have any verdict. That matches D-027. Not a bug."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/run.py", "line_start": 617, "line_end": 624, "title": "limit_hit aggregation scans runs and checks but misses waiting-suppressed timeouts", "why": "`hits` collects limit_hits from `runs` and `checks`; but `accepted` candidates may still be present for findings whose check timed out (they wouldn't). OK."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/run.py", "line_start": 496, "line_end": 503, "title": "Started timestamp of a check is set inside the worker, not guarded", "why": "`check.started = _utc_now()` is assigned inside `verify()` outside the lock. Since each check is verified by one worker only, this isn't a race, but `_record` uses `check.started or _now(...)`; if a check is popped by the thread but the review's finally block synthesizes a run for unfinished checks before the worker sets started, ordering is fine."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/run.py", "line_start": 356, "line_end": 373, "title": "fallback when no time is left to judge doesn't surface the reason in step", "why": "When `left <= 0`, `fallbacks.append('no time left to judge the merge')` and the merge step note gets this. That's fine."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/schedule.py", "line_start": 27, "line_end": 28, "title": "Robustness and nit share the same priority; nits should never reach verification", "why": "`_VERIFY` maps both \"robustness\" and \"nit\" to 3, so the docstring claim \"verify 🔵\" is conflated with nits. In practice nits skip verification in run_review, so nit is never used via verify_priority; but that has the fragile invariant that callers must pre-filter nits. If any future caller asks `verify_priority('nit')` for ordering, it silently gets robustness priority and can starve dimension turns. More importantly, `_VERIFY` includes an entry the docstring doesn't mention and the test `test_verifying_comes_before_finding_more_and_robustness_after` doesn't cover the nit confusion."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/schedule.py", "line_start": 40, "line_end": 41, "title": "Slots._free is decremented before popping and uses front-of-heap check, but waiters of same priority served FIFO only by heap tuple", "why": "The condition `while not (self._free > 0 and self._waiting[0] == me)` means only the head of the heap may proceed. If the current head has a lower priority number (higher priority) but is not runnable (e.g. it is waiting on a slot and _free == 0), it blocks correctly. But before the waiter that just acquired the slot decrements _free, it calls `self._changed.notify_all()`. A second waiter could wake, see _free still 1 (before the first decremented), and also pass its `self._waiting[0] == me` test if the first popped itself first — but the first pops itself before decrementing, so by the time notify is called the first has decremented. Ordering is OK. However `held` re-checks after `wait`, so it works."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/agent.py", "line_start": 165, "line_end": 170, "title": "Slot default `nullcontext` is an object, not a callable factory", "why": "`slot: Slot = nullcontext` where `Slot = Callable[[], AbstractContextManager]`. `nullcontext` itself is a class; calling `nullcontext()` returns a context manager, so callers do `with slot():` which calls `nullcontext()`. That is correct. But `slot` default binds the class; using it as `slot=lambda: self.slots.held(...)` works. Not a bug."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/agent.py", "line_start": 201, "line_end": 218, "title": "Time measurement moved inside slot but budget/exception paths return while holding the slot context", "why": "The `with slot():` block contains `return end` statements for the deadline-passed, BudgetExceeded, and generic exception cases. Returning inside the `with` releases the slot (since it will call __exit__), so the slot is properly released. Not a bug."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/agent.py", "line_start": 205, "line_end": 210, "title": "Deadline check reports 'time' limit even after slot wait that exceeded deadline", "why": "Once the slot is acquired and `left <= 0`, the loop returns limit_hit='time'. The agent_run then reports incomplete. That is intended."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/run.py", "line_start": 633, "line_end": 636, "title": "verifier_for_without verifier model uses finder model lambda but the settings verifier_model may exist while verifier_func is None", "why": "In `review_handler`, `verifier_for=(lambda left: chat_model(verifier, time_left=left)) if verifier else None`. If `verifier` (the chat model built from `settings.verifier_model`) exists, verifier_for uses the verifier model. If it doesn't exist but `settings.verifier_model` was configured, chat_model(settings.verifier_model) would have raised earlier. Fine. But if a verifier model exists yet `judge_for` and `verifier_for` use the *same* `verifier` model endpoint, the verifier model verifies findings it may have generated? No, dimension agents use finder. OK."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/run.py", "line_start": 487, "line_end": 500, "title": "when verifying is False (quick mode) findings are appended to accepted but no verdict, published.reported set", "why": "In quick mode, `verifying` is False so all non-nit findings go into `accepted` and `published.reported[candidate.id] = finding.severity`. Later `_insert_finding` looks up `published.verdicts.get(lead.id)` which is None for these; writes verdict=None. Fine for quick mode. But nits in normal mode also go via this path; that is documented."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/run.py", "line_start": 393, "line_end": 398, "title": "D-027 failure check runs even when verifying is False", "why": "`if checks and not any(...)` — when quick mode, checks is empty (nothing submitted for verification), so no failure. Correct."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/run.py", "line_start": 342, "line_end": 349, "title": "The verifier-model note is added whenverifier_for is None but verifying is true, but verifier_for defaults to model_for which is set", "why": "In run_review's signature, `verifier_for: ModelFor | None = None`. When verifying and verifier_for is None, the note is emitted and then `_Work.verifier_for = verifier_for or model_for`. The note is correct (finder verifies). However `review_handler` already passes verifier_for or None based on whether `verifier` exists. When settings.verifier_model is None, review_handler passes None so the note fires — that's the intent. Fine."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/merge.py", "line_start": 62, "line_end": 62, "title": "overlaps is now public but no doc change in signature/docs; is used from run.py without guarding against None", "why": "Renamed `_overlaps` to `overlaps`, imported into run.py. run.py calls `overlaps(m.finding, candidate.finding)` and expects boolean. No behaviour change."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/config.py", "line_start": 96, "line_end": 106, "title": "Verifier window check compares only `context_tokens`; the finder side input could use output_reserve etc", "why": "If the finder model and verifier model are the same object (verifier unset), the validator returns quickly. If verifier.context_tokens == finder.context_tokens but the verifier is at a *different* base_url with different output reserve expectations, the conversation budget should still be adequate. OK."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/config.py", "line_start": 96, "line_end": 106, "title": "Self-import model_validator / Self not shown; assume imported", "why": "The diff does not show `model_validator` and `Self` being imported. If they were already imported (Self exists if Python >=3.11 typing), and model_validator is from pydantic, likely present. Cannot verify from diff; could be a missing import that won't compile. Marked as a possible issue."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/run.py", "line_start": 460, "line_end": 463, "title": "finders/verifiers pools sized at model_concurrency each and shutdown(wait=False) leaves running verify() threads to still hold slots/emit events after find_and_verify returns", "why": "After the `finally` shuts down pools with `wait=False`, threads still in `verify()` continue running until they hit their deadline and then `events.put(...)`. The consumer loop has already exited (because `not (agents_out or checking)`). Those late `events.put` calls just fill the queue; but worse, `verify()` calls `self._record`? No — `_record` is called by the consumer. However `verify()` calls `heapq.heappop(self.pending)` and `UsageMeter` and writes to the DB via `review_usage`? And `run_verifier` may `_step`? No — steps for verify are written in `_record` by the consumer. `run_verifier` doesn't write to DB. But `UsageMeter` *does* call `review_usage` on the db_path connection potentially concurrent with the subsequent `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` in run_review — sqlite connection per call likely fine. Still, threads outliving the function keep using `self` and the review is marked done while verifiers may still be running, consuming tokens after the review's transaction. That is a real reliability problem: token accounting after DONE."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/run.py", "line_start": 405, "line_end": 407, "title": "A check queued but whose verify thread never starts before shutdown has run=None and gets 'deadline passed' reason", "why": "In the finally block of find_and_verify `pool.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)`: futures canceled before starting never run `verify()`. After the loop, `for check in checks: if check.run is None: ...` sets 'deadline passed before it was verified' with limit_hit='time'. Correct handling."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/run.py", "line_start": 545, "line_end": 549, "title": "For attachments to an existing check after its verdict: _accept is called with only the new candidate but the new candidate's `started` / `run` never gets the verdict set on it", "why": "When `same.run is not None and same.run.verdict is not None`, we call `_accept(same, [candidate], accepted, published)` which pushes the candidate into accepted with verdict severity. published.verdicts[candidate.id] and reported set. That's correct. But we also appended to `same.members`. Later, the outer loop on the existing check's completion already occurred (run.verdict existed), so no double-processing. Fine."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/run.py", "line_start": 619, "line_end": 620, "title": "checks that timed out are still in `checks` and the D-027 check sees them as None run — but they do have run set to a synthetic VerificationRun with verdict None", "why": "Synthetic run assigned in the post-loop `for check in checks`. So `c.run is not None` for all. The `any(c.run.verdict is not None ...)` correctly requires at least one real verdict. Good."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/run.py", "line_start": 470, "line_end": 475, "title": "The consumer thread blocks on queue.get with timeout computed from submit_by vs deadline; when a verify finishes before submit_by it is processed, but the finder completion does not wake the queue if no future comes", "why": "If `checking` becomes true and there are pending verifications but all finders are done (unlikely), the loop waits on events with deadline timeout; events will come from verifier futures. If a verifier is still running (slot blocked), the consumer waits until deadline and exits; correct."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/run.py", "line_start": 411, "line_end": 420, "title": "`self.candidates += 1` in _candidates is called from the consumer thread only — safe; but multiple find futures are consumed serially in the consumer", "why": "Since _candidates is only called from the consumer thread, no race. But the design intended candidate id assignment stable; IDs are assigned on consumption order rather than deterministic job order. That could vary run-to-run and affect fingerprint-based merge ordering, but is documented? Actually candidate ordering matters for the judge listing. Not a bug per se."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/pipeline/run.py", "line_start": 424, "line_end": 428, "title": "Self.starts written from finder threads without lock", "why": "`self.starts[job.node] = _utc_now()` in `find(job)` runs on a finder thread; `starts.get` is read in consumer thread for missing jobs. dict is not thread-safe in CPython for arbitrary operations under mutation, but simple assignments and get are effectively atomic. Still, race in reading while another thread may concurrently write is benign here (different keys per job)."}]}
